rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bursevi glosses تركنا as making or setting, and depicts all creatures mingling in bewilderment like turbulent sea waves when the promise begins.
rows.anchor: الترك الجعل كأنه ضد أي : وجعلنا {بعضهم} بعض الخلائق

rows.speaker: الإرشاد
rows.claim: The gathering blast is the second blast; the first is omitted to keep the events of the two lives connected without interruption.
rows.anchor: لعل ذلك قبل النفخة الأولى {ونفخ فى الصور} هي النفخة الثانية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Israfil breathes souls into bodies ready to receive them, like tinder ready to catch fire; the resurrected imagine their former lives were dreams, while the afterlife is true waking without sleep.
rows.anchor: نفخ إسرافيل في الصور أرواح الخلائق عند استعداد صور الأجساد لقبول الأرواح

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report describes the trumpet as a horn of light placed in Israfil's mouth.
rows.anchor: وسئل رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عن الصور فقال : "هو قرن من نور ألقمه إسرافيل".

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The vast trumpet contains corporeal images in which souls perceive real postmortem events; images differ in freedom of action, and some can look toward this world.
rows.anchor: لا شيء من الأكوان أوسع منه وإذا قبض الله الأرواح من هذه الأجسام الطبيعية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: True dreams occur in the sleeper's imaginal realm; the dream is sound but an interpreter errs by missing its intended meaning. Pharaoh's people are shown fire there before entering its bodily punishment at Resurrection.
rows.anchor: وهو الذي يصدق رؤياه أبدا وكل رؤيا صادقة ولا تخطى ولكن العابر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All creatures, including angels, humans, jinn, and animals, are gathered on one plain after their bodies are reassembled for judgment and recompense.
rows.anchor: جمعنا الخلائق بعدما تمزقت أجسادهم في صعيد واحد للحساب والجزاء

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report says the fortunate person in that vast gathering is whoever can find room to set down his toes.
rows.anchor: وفي الحديث : "السعيد في ذلك اليوم في ذلك الجمع من يجد مكانا يضع عليه أصابع رجليه"

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: The same trumpet is the means of death at the first blast and life at the last, displaying God's power to make one cause produce opposite outcomes.
rows.anchor: من كمال قدرته يحيي الخلق بسبب يميتهم به وهو النفخة وبالنفخة الأولى

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: Creatures must use causes to reach things, but only God, the maker of causes, can make one thing cause two opposites such as death and life.
rows.anchor: الخلق محتاجون إلى اتباع سبب كل شيء ليبلغوا إليه وهم لا يقدرون

rows.speaker: المثنوي
rows.claim: The cited verses portray the inner song of saints as a present-day Israfil: divine summons revives spiritually dead hearts, though the sense-bound ear cannot hear it.
rows.anchor: هين كه اسرافيل وقتند اوليا مرده را زيشان حياتست ونما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: عرض means to show or make manifest; Hell is shown to the gathered disbelievers, who see and hear its rage and roaring in a display whose terror cannot be fathomed.
rows.anchor: عرض الشيء له أظهره أي : أظهرنا {جهنم} معرب والأصل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some say the name Jahannam is non-Arabic, originally ه نم.
rows.anchor: معرب والأصل (ه نم) كذا قال البعض

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A Prophetic report says Hell is brought with seventy thousand reins, each drawn by seventy thousand angels; it is set so the only route to Paradise is across the bridge.
rows.anchor: يؤتى بجهنم يومئذ لها سبعون ألف زمام مع كل زمام سبعون ألف ملك يجرونها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although everyone at the gathering can see Hell, its display is directed especially at disbelievers and itself punishes them with overwhelming grief.
rows.anchor: وتخصيص العرض بالكافرين مع أنها بمرأى من أهل الجمع قاطبة لأن ذلك لأجلهم خاصة

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: Had disbelieving souls seen Hell before Judgment as believers did, they would have believed, since their eyes were uncovered from remembrance and their hearts could hear God's speech.
rows.anchor: لو كانت معروضة على أرواح الكافرين قبل يوم القيامة كما كانت معروضة على أرواح المؤمنين

rows.speaker: الكواشي
rows.claim: The relative clause describes or substitutes for the disbelievers, so there is no pause after عرضا.
rows.anchor: الموصول مع صلته نعت للكافرين أو بدل ولذا لا وقف على عرضا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their eyes were covered by a thick veil from the signs that lead reflective observers to God's remembrance through affirmation of unity and glorification.
rows.anchor: غلاف غليظ محاطة بذلك من جميع الجوانب.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They could not hear because they fiercely shut themselves off from truth and opposed the Messenger; their condition exceeded ordinary deafness, which may still hear a shout.
rows.anchor: لفرط تصاممهم عن الحق وكمال عداوتهم للرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: الإرشاد
rows.claim: The veiled eyes picture their disregard of visible proofs, while inability to hear pictures rejection of proofs received by hearing.
rows.anchor: وهذا تمثيل لإعراضهم عن الأدلة السمعية كما أن الأول تصوير لتعاميهم عن الآيات المشاهدة

rows.speaker: بعض الكبار
rows.claim: Inwardly, the souls are veiled by heedlessness, hearts by worldly desire, secrets by attention to the two worlds, and spirits by remembering other-than-God.
rows.anchor: كانت أعين نفوسهم في غطاء الغفلة عن نظر العبرة وأعين قلوبهم في غطاء حب الدنيا

rows.speaker: بعض الكبار
rows.claim: Opening the inner eye through direct witnessing opens the outer eye to reflection; outward hearing follows inward hearing, which includes the Prophet's Sunnah and the lives of the righteous.
rows.anchor: فإذا فتحت العين الباطنة بالمشاهدة فتحت العين الظاهرة بنظر الاعتبار وكذا السمع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The interrogative hamza reproaches and denies the act; the fa connects the rebuke to an implied premise: did they disbelieve despite God's majesty and then suppose this?
rows.anchor: الهمزة للإنكار والتوبيخ على معنى إنكار الواقع واستقباحه كما في قولك أضربت أباك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's servants here are angels, Jesus, and Ezra, all under His sovereignty; taking them as guardians means worshipping them and seeking their protection from God's punishment.
rows.anchor: من الملائكة وعيسى وعزير وهم تحت سلطاني وملكوتي {من دونى} مجاوزين إياي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bursevi prefers that the supposed guardians are objects of worship: the alleged taking is no real mutual alliance, since the servants disavow their worshippers and say God alone is their protector.
rows.anchor: وهم عليهم السلام منزهون عن ولايتهم بالمرة لقولهم سبحانك أنت ولينا من دونهم

rows.speaker: الإرشاد
rows.claim: An alternative supplies an omitted second object: the unbelievers thought taking guardians would benefit them; Bursevi rejects it because it concedes some reality to the taking.
rows.anchor: وقيل مفعوله الثاني محذوف أي : أفحسبوا اتخاذهم نافعا لهم والوجه هو الأول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God prepared Hell as a guest's lodging for the disbelievers; the word is taunting and hints that further punishment awaits beyond Hell.
rows.anchor: هيأناها {للكافرين} المعهودين {نزلا} وهو ما يعد للنزيل والضيف أي : أحضرنا جهنم للكافرين

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas explains نزلا as a place of descent and abode.
rows.anchor: وفسره ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما بموضع النزول والمثوى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The worse punishment is being veiled from seeing God; the sequence in the cited passage places being burned after veiling, so burning is lower in rank.
rows.anchor: جعل الصلي أي : الدخول تاليا في المرتبة للمحجوبية فهو دونها في الرتبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One who claims God's love and loyalty cannot take other allies; those who reject divine friendship and attach themselves to others face the Hell of distance and separation.
rows.anchor: من ادعى محبة الله وولاءه لا يتخذ من دون الله أولياء إذ لا يجتمع ولاية الحق وولاية الخلق

rows.speaker: بعض المحققين
rows.claim: Love will not use a lover for anyone besides the beloved; love of God is the axis of goodness, shown by obeying commands and avoiding prohibitions.
rows.anchor: أبت المحبة أن تستعمل محبا لغير محبوبه وحب الله تعالى قطب تدور عليه الخيرات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Disbelievers wasted life in sin and worship of what is not truly existent, while believers trained themselves in obedience and worshipped only the Real; therefore the former receive Hell and the latter high ranks.
rows.anchor: فالذين كفروا أضاعوا أيامهم بالكفر والآثام وعبدوا المعدوم وهو ما سوى الله الملك العلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A story tells of a tyrant polytheist imprisoned in a heated vessel who converted and prayed; rain and wind freed him, and his people converted after witnessing God's power.
rows.anchor: حكي أنه كان ملك مشرك جبار فأخذه المسلمون فجعلوه في قمقمة ووضعوها في نار شديدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement explains the preceding matter: Hell is their recompense for disbelief, denial of what they owed belief, and ridicule of revealed books and God's messengers.
rows.anchor: {بما كفروا واتخذوا ءاياتى ورسلى هزوا}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling the signs and messengers mockery is an intensified verbal-noun description, or means they were objects of ridicule or a place of mockery.
rows.anchor: من قبيل الوصف بالمصدر للمبالغة يعني أنهم بالغوا في الاستهزاء بآيات الله ورسله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As practicing scholars inherit prophets' knowledge and deeds, those who mock prophets inherit the mockery and error of Abu Jahl, Uqba, and their peers.
rows.anchor: العلماء العاملين ورثة الأنبياء والمرسلين في علومهم وأعمالهم كذلك المستهزؤن بهم ورثة أبي جهل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bursevi recounts that Abu Jahl mocked the Prophet by contorting his nose and mouth behind him; the Prophet told him to remain so, and he did until death.
rows.anchor: ومن استهزاء أبي جهل بالنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه كان يخلج بأنفه وفمه خلف رسول الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bursevi says Uqba spat in the Prophet's face, but it turned back and gave him leprosy; he links Uqba to the warning in 25:27 and says he eats his hands in Hell.
rows.anchor: ومن استهزاء عقبة به عليه السلام أنه بصق يوما في وجه النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report says a gate of Paradise is opened to mockers and they are beckoned, then it is shut as they arrive; the cycle continues until they no longer come.
rows.anchor: يفتح لأحدهم باب من الجنة فيقال هلم هلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The believers are those who trusted in worldly life and performed deeds sincerely for God's sake.
rows.anchor: في الدنيا {وعملوا الصالحات} من الأعمال وهي ما كانت خالصة لوجه الله تعالى

rows.speaker: القاموس
rows.claim: Firdaws means an orchard containing the varied plants of gardens, especially vines; the word may be feminine and Arabic or borrowed from Greek or Syriac.
rows.anchor: الفردوس البستان يجمع كل ما يكون في البساتين يكون فيه الكروم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Grammatically, nuzul is the predicate and means lodging prepared for a guest: the gardens, their fruits, or the whole garden itself can be called the welcome gift to stress honor.
rows.anchor: والنزل المنزل وما هيىء للضيف النازل أي : كانت جنات الفردوس منازل مهيأة لهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because God prepared for the righteous what no eye saw, no ear heard, and no heart imagined, the gardens are only the lodging before a greater divine hospitality.
rows.anchor: أعددت لعبادي الصالحين ما لا عين رأت ولا أذن سمعت ولا خطر على قلب بشر

rows.speaker: الكاشفي
rows.claim: Kashifi calls Firdaws the state of meeting God; the cited Hafiz verse contrasts the ascetic's Garden blessing with the beloved's face and values each by aspiration.
rows.anchor: قال الكاشفي : هي دولة اللقاء ، قال الحافظ : نعمت فردوس زاهد راوما راروى دوست

rows.speaker: أبو يزيد البسطامي
rows.claim: Abu Yazid says even punishment would leave him occupied with Paradise and its delights; no Garden surpasses meeting and union, and no fire exceeds separation.
rows.anchor: ومن هنا قال أبو يزيد البسطامي قدس سره لو عذبني الله يوم القيامة لشغلني بالجنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The inhabitants are destined to remain in the Gardens and will not seek to leave for another place, since no place is better and every desire is met.
rows.anchor: لا يطلبون تحولا وانتقالا عنها إلى غيرها كما ينتقل الرجل من دار إذا لم توافقه إلى دار

rows.speaker: الإمام
rows.claim: The Imam says this quality marks complete felicity: in worldly life a person at any happy station still longs for a higher one.
rows.anchor: وهذا الوصف يدل على غاية الكمال لأن الإنسان في الدنيا إذا وصل إلى أي درجة

rows.speaker: تفسير الشيخ
rows.claim: The Sheikh's commentary allows that the phrase denies any transition and reinforces eternal abiding, making it a metaphor for immortality.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يراد نفي التحول وتأكيد الخلود كما في "تفسير الشيخ" وهذا كناية عن التخليد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Firdaws is described as the highest, finest green hill in Paradise, the Garden's center; a report says it is the highest of one hundred levels, its rivers spring from it, and the Throne is above it.
rows.anchor: الفردوس أعلاها فيها تتفجر الأنهار الأربعة وفوقها عرش الرحمن فإذا سألتم الله فاسألوا الفردوس

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report describes two Firdaws gardens with silver vessels and contents and two with gold vessels and contents.
rows.anchor: جنتان الفردوس أربع جنات من فضة آنيتهما وما فيهما فضة وجنتان من ذهب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bursevi reconciles reports of nine daily looks at Firdaws and five by treating the first as detailed and the second as summary; the increase follows the five prayers, originally fifty at the Ascension.
rows.anchor: التوفيق بين الروايتين أن الأولى من مقام التفصيل والثانية من مقام الإجمال

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: One report bars habitual wine drinkers and dayyuths from Firdaws; Bursevi defines a dayyuth as one who accepts sexual immorality among his family.
rows.anchor: وعزتي وجلالي لا يدخلها مدمن خمر ولا ديوث

rows.speaker: بحر العلوم
rows.claim: Another report describes God building Firdaws with gold and musk bricks, planting fruit and fragrance, and making rivers; no habitual wine drinker or persistent adulterer enters.
rows.anchor: قال عليه السلام : "إن الله كبس عرصة جنة الفردوس بيده ثم بناها لبنة من ذهب مصفى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bursevi answers that the supreme Firdaws is for those combining complete eyewitness faith, inward sincerity, and outward Sharia observance; the qualification also includes commanding right and forbidding wrong.
rows.anchor: يؤول العنوان بمن جمع بين الإيمان والعمل على وجه الكمال وهو بأن آمن إيمانا عيانيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The believers are the opposite of those who rejected God's signs and meeting; their faith rises from unseen evidence to direct vision and witnessing, supported by the next verse's call to hope for meeting.
rows.anchor: فإن المراد بيان المؤمنين المتصفين بأضداد ما اتصفوا به والإيمان باللقاء أي : الرؤية والمشهود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bursevi prays for Firdaws together with the vision of God's beauty and the joy of union.
rows.anchor: نسأل الله الفردوس بل وتجلي جماله والاحتظاظ بكاسات وصاله

rows.speaker: الحافظ
rows.claim: The cited Hafiz poem says the lover of God's street needs no eight Gardens and is freed from both worlds by love.
rows.anchor: كداى كوى تو ازهشت خلد مستغنيست اسير عشق تو ازهردو كون آزادست

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sea's like means another sea like the existing one, and مددا is an accusative of specification meaning additional help; even the added sea would run out, while God's words do not.
rows.anchor: بمثله} بمثل البحر الموجود يعني بمائة. وقال الكاشفي : (واكرنيز بياريم مثل درياى محيط) {مددا} تمييز أي زيادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bursevi prefers making the omitted result explicit as God's words would not run out even with another sea, because this matches 31:27 and directly contrasts finite sea with inexhaustible words.
rows.anchor: وهو أحسن لكونه أوفق بقوله : {ولو أنما فى الارض من شجرة أقلام والبحر يمده منا بعده سبعة أبحر ما نفدت كلمات الله}

rows.speaker: الإرشاد
rows.claim: The final clause is God's own confirming statement; finite seas and all existing bodies are bounded, as proven by the finitude of dimensions.
rows.anchor: من الأجسام لا يكون إلا متناهيا لقيام الأدلة القاطعة على تناهي الابعاد

rows.speaker: الإمام
rows.claim: God's capacity can always create more after any point, while this does not imply that an actually infinite collection of possible things exists.
rows.anchor: معناه أن قادرية الله تعالى لا تنتهي إلى حد إلا ويصح منه الإيجاد بعد ذلك انتهى أي : فلا يلزم منه عدم تناهي الممكنات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bursevi's teacher takes God's words as expressions of His knowledge and wisdom; the sea truly runs out, but divine words have no actual exhaustion.
rows.anchor: قوله كلمات علمه وحكمته الظاهر أن المراد الكلمات التي يعبر بها عن معلومات الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bursevi raises an objection: if words mean finite knowables, they too seem finite; if they mean unknowables, that would imply impossible ignorance in God.
rows.anchor: فكيف يتم ما ذكرتم إذ كل منهما مما ينفد ويتناهى فههنا اشكال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muhammad is human like his audience in bodily form and some human traits, yet God favored him alone among them with prophethood and revelation.
rows.anchor: ما أنا إلا آدمي مثلكم في الصورة ومساو بكم في بعض الصفات البشرية {يوحى إلى} من ربي

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: All humans share human nature and capacity; they differ through faith, sainthood, prophethood, revelation, and knowledge that God is uniquely one and self-subsisting.
rows.anchor: بني آدم في البشرية واستعداد الإنسانية سواء النبي والولي والمؤمن والكافر

rows.speaker: الإرشاد
rows.claim: Here kāna denotes continuity and hope anticipates future arrival; meeting one's Lord means expecting His favor.
rows.anchor: كان للاستمرار ولرجاء توقع وصول الخبر في المستقبل والمراد بلقائه كرامته

rows.speaker: الإمام
rows.claim: The Imam says the Asharis interpret meeting the Lord as seeing Him, while the Mu'tazilites take it as meeting His reward; the root can mean to see.
rows.anchor: أصحابنا حملوا لقاء الرب على رؤيته والمعتزلة على لقاء ثوابه يقال لقيه كرضيه رآه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A sound deed is done to attain the desired meeting; al-Antaki says one who fears standing before God should do what is fit to present, with hope also meaning fear or expectation.
rows.anchor: من خاف المقام بين أيدي الله فليعمل عملا يصلح للعرض عليه والرجاء يكون بمعنى الخوف

rows.speaker: ذو النون
rows.claim: Dhu al-Nun defines the righteous deed as one free of ostentation.
rows.anchor: وقال ذو النون العمل الصالح هو الخالص من الرياء

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله القرشي
rows.claim: Abu Abd Allah al-Qurashi defines the righteous deed as one to which the ego gives no attention and from which it seeks neither reward nor recompense.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو عبد الله القرشي : العمل الصالح الذي ليس للنفس إليه التفات ولا به طلب ثواب

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: The inward reading defines good action as following the Prophet outwardly and inwardly; inward Sunnah is devotion to God and turning one's gaze from everything else.
rows.anchor: العمل الصالح متابعة النبي عليه السلام والتأسي بسنته ظاهرا وباطنا فأما سنة باطنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bursevi cites the Prophet's undistracted vision as evidence for inward devotion and turning wholly toward God.
rows.anchor: {ما زاغ البصر وما طغى} (النجم : 17)

rows.speaker: أبو البقاء
rows.claim: Abu al-Baqa allows the phrase to mean either in the worship of his Lord or because of that worship.
rows.anchor: قال أبو البقاء أي : في عبادة ربه ويجوز أن يكون على بابه أي : بسبب عبادة ربه

rows.speaker: الإرشاد
rows.claim: The warning covers overt association like the disbelievers' and hidden association such as ostentation or seeking a reward through worship.
rows.anchor: إشراكا جليا كما فعله الذين كفروا بآيات ربهم ولقائه ولا إشراكا خفيا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas explains that the wording targets deeds a person performs and wants others to praise.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما لم يقل ولا يشرك به لأنه أراد العمل الذي يعمله

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan applies the verse to sharing an act intended for God with people; Jundub ibn Zuhayr said he was pleased when others saw his worship, and reports give both rejection and two rewards depending on intention.
rows.anchor: وعن الحسن هذا فيمن أشرك بعمل يريد الله به والناس على ما روى أن جندب بن زهير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Being pleased that worship is seen earns reward when the aim is to set a good example or avoid suspicion over an obligation; seeking praise and fame alone is ostentation, so concealment protects the deed.
rows.anchor: فأما إذا أراد به مجرد مدح الناس وانتشار الصيت والذكر فهو محض الرياء والشرك

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن غالب
rows.claim: Abd Allah ibn Ghalib publicly mentioned his nightly recitation and prayer, citing the command to speak of God's favor; Bursevi permits this to encourage others if one is safe from temptation, though concealment is better.
rows.anchor: وعن عبد الله بن غالب أنه كان إذا أصبح يقول رزقني الله البارحة خيرا قرأت كذا وصليت كذا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse gathers the two foundations of knowledge and action: monotheism and sincerity, illustrated by Sa'di's contrast between sincere devotion and ostentatious religious dress.
rows.anchor: والآية جامعة لخلاصتي العلم والعمل وهما التوحيد والإخلاص في العمل

rows.speaker: بحر العلوم
rows.claim: Bahr al-Ulum defines ostentation as acting for someone other than God and cites a report that the Prophet feared such deeds more than worship of idols or celestial bodies.
rows.anchor: إن أخوف ما أخاف على أمتي الإشراك بالله أما أني لا أقول يعبدون شمسا ولا قمرا

rows.speaker: الأشباه
rows.claim: Al-Ashbah says ostentation does not enter fasting unless the faster displays its effects or hints at it.
rows.anchor: قال في "الأشباه" : ولا يدخل الرياء في الصوم انتهى هذا إذا لم يجوع نفسه إظهارا لأثره

rows.speaker: عبادة بن الصامت
rows.claim: Ubadah ibn al-Samit transmits that prayer or fasting done for show is association, and the Prophet recited this verse; the same principle extends to charity, pilgrimage, and other good works.
rows.anchor: على ما روي عن عبادة بن الصامت رضي الله عنه قال : سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول : "من صلى صلاة يرائي بها فقد أشرك

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report warns that God forbids Paradise to every ostentatious person and values humility and composure above fine dress.
rows.anchor: وفي الحديث : "إنما حرم الله لجنة على كل مرائى" ليس البر في حسن اللباس والزي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bursevi cites poetry that judges people by character and conduct, not outward dress, and says even a sinful night-thief is preferable to the ostentatious person who leads others astray.
rows.anchor: كراجامه اكست وسيرت ليد در دوز خش را نبايد كليد

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report at the Resurrection tells anyone who partnered another in an act to seek its reward from that partner, since God needs no partners.
rows.anchor: فليطلب ثواب عمله من عند غير الله فإن الله أغنى الشركاء عن الشرك

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Reports describe a valley in Hell prepared for ostentatious people and identify ostentation as lesser shirk and the hidden shirk most feared for the community.
rows.anchor: وفي الحديث : "إن في جهنم واديا تستعيذ جهنم من ذلك الوادي في كل يوم مائة مرة

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report says hidden shirk is subtler than an ant on stone in a dark night and teaches a prayer for refuge from knowingly associating and forgiveness for unwitting association.
rows.anchor: فإن الشرك أخفى من دبيب النمل على الصفا في الليلة الظلماء" فشق على الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah is Meccan and has ninety-eight or ninety-nine verses, excepting the prostration verse.
rows.anchor: ثمان أو تسع وتسعون آية وهي مكية إلا آية السجدة

rows.speaker: الإرشاد
rows.claim: Kaf Ha Ya Ayn Sad is the surah's name and nominative predicate of an omitted demonstrative; pointing to it is valid because it is treated as present, like saying this is what someone bought.
rows.anchor: اسم للسورة ومحله الرفع على أنه خبر لمبتدأ محذوف والتقدير هذا كهيعص

rows.speaker: تفسير الشيخ
rows.claim: The Sheikh's commentary takes the letters as an oath, a divine name, or a compound whose letters indicate attributes: generosity, guidance, mercy, knowledge, might, and truthfulness.
rows.anchor: قسم اقسم بالله تعالى أو هي اسم من اسمائه الحسهنى

rows.speaker: تفسير الشيخ
rows.claim: The letters may also express that God suffices His creatures, guides His servants, has power over them, knows creation, and fulfills His promise.
rows.anchor: أو معناه هو تعالى كاف لخلقه هاد لعباده يده فوق أيديهم عالم ببريته صادق في وعده

rows.speaker: الكاشفي
rows.claim: Kashifi transmits Simnani's teaching that the Prophet has human, angelic, and divine modes: compound words belong to the human mode, separate letters to the angelic mode, and obscure speech to the divine mode.
rows.anchor: حضرت رسالت را صلى الله عليه وسلم سه صورتست يكى بشرى كقوله تعالى : {إنمآ أنا بشر مثلكم}

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: The separated letters may be a private alphabet of love agreed between God and His Prophet, unknowable to others and spoken through Gabriel.
rows.anchor: من قبيل المواضعات والمعميات بالحروف بين المحبين لا يطلع عليها غيرهم وقد واضعها الله تعالى مع نبيه

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: A report says Gabriel recited the letters one at a time and the Prophet recognized each; Gabriel asked how he knew what Gabriel himself did not know.
rows.anchor: فلما قال كاف قال النبي عليه السلام : "علمت" فقال ها فقال : "علمت"

rows.speaker: أسئلة الحكم
rows.claim: Quranic knowledge is divided into what God keeps to Himself, secrets disclosed exclusively to the Prophet or an authorized person, and meanings God taught the Prophet to teach; opening letters belong to the second category or, by another view, the first.
rows.anchor: علم لم يطلع الله عليه أحدا من خلقه وهو ما استأثر به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The recited passage is called a remembrance; mercy is in an objective genitive relation to remembrance, servant is the object of mercy, and Zakariyya is its apposition.
rows.anchor: ذكر مضاف إلى مفعوله {عبده} مفعول رحمة {زكريآ} بدل منه

rows.speaker: الكاشفي
rows.claim: Kashifi says Zakariyya descended from Rehoboam, Solomon, and David, was a high-ranking prophet and leader of Jerusalem's priests, and served at the sacrifice.
rows.anchor: قال الكاشفي : (واو ازاولاد رجعيم بن سليمان بن داود عليهم السلام بوده بيغمبر عاليشان

rows.speaker: الإمام
rows.claim: The Imam traces Zakariyya to Aaron, brother of Moses, through Levi, Jacob, and Isaac.
rows.anchor: قال الإمام زكريا من ولد هارون أخي موسى وهما من ولد لاوى بن يعقوب بن إسحاق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zakariyya prayed quietly in the Jerusalem sanctuary after making an offering; secrecy showed good manners, sincerity, and freedom from show, hid his request from hostile relatives, and spared him public censure over seeking a child in old age.
rows.anchor: ولقد راعى عليه السلام حسن الأدب في دعائه فإنه مع كونه بالنسبة إليه تعالى كالجهر أدخل في الإخلاص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bursevi answers the apparent paradox that a call is loud: Zakariyya prayed during ritual prayer and kept his voice low; even a faint voice can be called hidden speech.
rows.anchor: قلت دعا في الصلاة فاخفاه.

rows.speaker: الفناري
rows.claim: Al-Fanari notes that jurists count some quiet recitation as the lowest degree of audible speech.
rows.anchor: وقد صح عن الفقهاء أن بعض المخافتة يعد من أدنى مراتب الجهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For spiritual elites, hidden invocation is what the recording angels cannot hear, not simply a lowered voice; calling it a call conveys intense attention to God, as with prophets and perfected saints.
rows.anchor: النداء الخفي عند الخواص كالذكر الخفي هو ما خفي عن الحفظة فضلا عن الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Weakness means frailty; bone is singled out as the body's support, so if its least-affected, firmest part weakens the rest of the body is affected too.
rows.anchor: لأنه عماد بيت البدن فإذا أصابه الضعف مع صلابته

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says Zakariyya complained that his teeth had fallen out; the singular bone names the whole kind and conveys that every bone was weak.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة : اشتكى سقوط الأضراس كما في البغوي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase منّي specifies the bone after the general statement, adding emphasis; the possessive relation is already implied by the context.
rows.anchor: {منى} متعلق بمحذوف وهو حال من العظم وهو تفصيل بعد الإجمال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The head is said to flare gray: deletion leaves 'my head', while the image compares white, shining gray hair and its spread through the roots to flame, stressing that no black hair remained.
rows.anchor: شبه الشيب في بياضه وإنارته بشواظ النار وانتشاره في الشعر ومنبته مبالغة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Making gray hair the specification reverses the ordinary order, as in saying a house caught fire rather than fire caught in a house.
rows.anchor: والأصل اشتعل شيب رأسي فوزانه بالنسبة إلى الأصل وزان اشتعل بيته نارا

rows.speaker: الشيخ سعدي
rows.claim: Sa'di's cited verses use gray hair to mark the passing of youth and life and urge the sleeper to wake before time is gone.
rows.anchor: وشيبت در آمد بروى شباب شبت روز شد ديده بركن زخواب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zakariyya feared what his relatives would do after his death; the implied object is their misrule, not the relatives themselves, since that would distort the meaning.
rows.anchor: أي بعد موتي فلا بد لي من الخلف وهو متعلق بمحذوف ينساق إليه الذهن أي جور الموالي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His bodily weakness and advanced age prompt fear that his paternal cousins, wicked Israelites, would mishandle his community and alter its religion.
rows.anchor: وكانوا شرار بني إسرائيل فخاف أن لا يحسنوا خلافته في أمته ويبدلوا عليهم دينهم

rows.speaker: القاموس
rows.claim: Qamus lists many senses of mawla, including owner, servant, freedman, companion, relative, neighbor, ally, son, uncle, and protector; here it means relatives.
rows.anchor: المولى المالك والعبد والمعتق والصاحب والقريب كابن العم ونحوه والجار والحليف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bursevi identifies the wife as Isya daughter of Faqudh and sister of Hanna, whom al-Tabari identifies as Mary's mother.
rows.anchor: هي ايشاع بنت فاقوذ بن فيل وهي أخت حنة بنت فاقوذ

rows.speaker: القتيبي
rows.claim: Al-Qutaybi identifies Zakariyya's wife as Isya daughter of Imran; on this view John is Jesus' literal maternal cousin, while the other view makes him Mary's mother's cousin.
rows.anchor: وقال القتيبي امرأة زكريا هي ايشاع بنت عمران فعلى هذا القول يكون يحيى ابن خالة عيسى

rows.speaker: الإمام السهيلي
rows.claim: Al-Suhayli favors the first genealogy because the Ascension report calls John and Jesus maternal cousins; the wife had been barren since youth and was ninety-eight, according to Kashifi.
rows.anchor: وفي حديث الإسراء : "فلقيت ابني الخالة يحيى وعيسى" وهذا شاهد للقول الأول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrases من لدنك and لي both attach to the request but carry different relations: min marks a figurative origin, and ladun names a starting point; he asks for a child by sheer grace beyond ordinary causes.
rows.anchor: كلا الجارين متعلق بهب لاختلاف مغييبها فاللام صلة له ومن لابتداء الغاية مجازا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wali means a son from his own loins who will succeed him in religious affairs.
rows.anchor: ولدا من صلبي يلي أمر الدين بعدي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The inheritance is knowledge, religion, and prophethood, not property, since the Prophet said prophets leave what they bequeath as charity.
rows.anchor: يرثني من حيث العلم والدين والنبوة فإن الأنبياء لا يورثون المال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bursevi poses the problem that John reportedly died before Zakariyya and answers that prophets' prayers are not always granted in every detail; God ordained John as a praised prophet but not as Zakariyya's heir.
rows.anchor: لكنهم ليسوا كذلك في جميع الدعوات حسبما تقتضيه المشيئة الإلهية المبنية على الحكم

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi and Muqatil identify the family of Jacob as Jacob son of Mathan, Mary's maternal grandfather; their clan ruled Israel and Zakariyya hoped his son would inherit priestly office and kingship.
rows.anchor: وقال الكلبي ومقاتل هو يعقوب بن ماثان أخو عمران بن ماثان من نسل سليمان عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aal means the close adherents whose affairs return to a person through kinship, companionship, or shared religion; 'make him pleasing' means pleasing in word and deed, with رب interposed to intensify supplication.
rows.anchor: وآل الرجل خاصة الذين يؤول إليه أمرهم للقرابة أو الصحبة أو الموافقة في الدين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God only opens the door of supplication to answer it wholly or partly; opening it is a sign that mercy's doors are opening because supplication displays need and humility, which God loves.
rows.anchor: لا يمكن العبد من الدعاء إلا لإجابته كلا أو بعضا كما وقع لزكريا

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report says that whoever is granted access to supplication has the doors of mercy opened.
rows.anchor: وفي الحديثك : "من فتح له باب الدعاء فتحت له أبواب الرحمة"

rows.speaker: أبو يزيد البسطامي
rows.claim: After thirty years of worship, Abu Yazid says he was told that reaching God requires poverty, helplessness, and need rather than more worship.
rows.anchor: كابدت العبادة ثلاثين سنة فرأيت قائلا يقول لي : يا أبا يزيد خزائنه مملوءة من العبادات

rows.speaker: بعض أهل المعرفة
rows.claim: A gnostic calls supplication the best weapon, fidelity the best mount, and weeping the best intercessor.
rows.anchor: نعم السلاح الدعاء ، ونعم المطية الوفاء ، ونعم الشفيع البكاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The perfected seek religious rather than worldly ends; Zakariyya asks for an heir of knowledge because worldly order depends on knowledge, action, piety, justice, and fairness.
rows.anchor: ثم إن الدعاء إما للدين أو للدنيا والأول مطمح نظر الكمل ألا ترى أن زكريا طلب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The perfect person of each age manifests divine lights and secrets; a seeker reaches God through such a person, and should ask for the best child whose remembrance endures to the Day of Calling.
rows.anchor: وجعل الإنسان الكامل في كل عصر مجلى أنواره ومظهر أسراره فمن أراد الوصول إلى الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The call to Zakariyya and glad tidings are grammatically introduced as the angel's speech; the same angelic call appears while Zakariyya is praying in the sanctuary.
rows.anchor: يا زكريا} على إرادة القول أي : قال تعالى على لسان الملك يا زكريا كما قال في سورة آل عمران

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zakariyya addresses God directly, although the news came through an angel, to intensify pleading and intimacy and avoid implying that God's knowledge depends on angelic mediation.
rows.anchor: ناداه تعالى بالذات مع وصول خطابه تعالى إليه بتوسط الملك للمبالغة في التضرع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His question is how or from where a son could come when his wife was barren in youth and he himself had reached extreme old age.
rows.anchor: لم تلد في شبابها وشبابي فكيف وهي عجوز الآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿItiyyan means dryness, like dry wood; it also describes a person who has grown old or anything that has reached its end.
rows.anchor: {عتيا} يبوسة وجفافا كالعود اليابس من قولهم عتا العود إذا يبس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zakariyya's amazement acknowledges God's complete power and the irrelevance of ordinary causes; the question expresses wonder by customary standards, not doubt about divine ability.
rows.anchor: اعترافا بأن المؤثر فيه كمال قدرته وأن الوسائط عند التحقيق ملغاة

rows.speaker: الإمام
rows.claim: The Imam says the couple may have been rejuvenated before conceiving or may have conceived in old age; 21:89–90 is evidence that his wife's reproductive strength was restored.
rows.anchor: تعجب من أن يجعلهما شابين ثم يرزقها الولد أو يتركهما شيخين ويلدان مع الشيخوخة

rows.speaker: الأسئلة المقحمة
rows.claim: Another explanation says Zakariyya asked whether the child would come from his currently barren wife, another wife, or a concubine.
rows.anchor: أراد من التي يكون منه هذا الولد أمن هذه المرة وهي عاقر أم من امرأة أخرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The angel replies that matters are as Zakariyya said; one reading says God restores his potency and opens his wife's womb despite their age.
rows.anchor: {كذالك} أي : الأمر كما قلت.

rows.speaker: الإرشاد
rows.claim: The kāf in كذلك may be extra, making the word a simile for God's prior promise; the statement that it is easy confirms and guarantees that promise. Alternatively, it predicates an omitted subject referring to the promise.
rows.anchor: الكاف في كذلك مقحمة كما في مثلك لا يبخل فمحلها النصب على أنه مصدر تشبيهي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God created Zakariyya before John when he was nothing; making a son from aged parents only changes attributes, easier than creating the person and attributes from nothing.
rows.anchor: والمراد خلق آدم لأنه أنموذج مشتمل على جميع الذرية

rows.speaker: الإمام
rows.claim: The Imam argues that creating an essence and its qualities from nonexistence is greater than changing qualities, so creating the child is within God's power.
rows.anchor: أن خلقه من العدم الصرف خلق للذات والصفات وخلق الولد من شيخين لا يحتاج إلا إلى تبديل الصفات

rows.speaker: بحر العلوم
rows.claim: Bahr al-Ulum says, according to our school, the word شيء applies only to what exists; denying that Zakariyya was a thing establishes his nonexistence.
rows.anchor: ولفظ الشيء عندنا يختص بالموجود وبالعكس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zakariyya asks for a sign that pregnancy has occurred so he can give thanks from its beginning; the question likely came after some interval, according to a report about John's relative age.
rows.anchor: علامة على وقوع الحبل لا تلقى تلك النعمة الجليلة بالشكر من حين حدوثها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The three nights without speaking to people did not prevent Zakariyya from remembering and glorifying God; specifying people indicates that only ordinary speech was withheld, and the parallel states three days too.
rows.anchor: مع القدرة على الذكر والتسبيح كما هو المفهوم من تخصيص الناس {ثلاث ليال}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says Zakariyya returned to his wife that night and conception occurred; the next morning he could not speak to people.
rows.anchor: رجع تلك الليلة إلى امرأته فقربها ووقع الولد في رحمها فلما أصبح امتنع عليه الكلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After his wife conceived, Zakariyya left the prayer room or chamber while his people waited outside; seeing him changed and silent, they asked what was wrong, and he gestured for them to pray or glorify God.
rows.anchor: {على قومه من المحراب} من المصلى أو من الغرفة وكانوا من وراء المحراب ينتظرون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Morning runs from dawn to forenoon and evening from noon until sunset; the two terms mark the times for glorification.
rows.anchor: {بكرة} هي من طلوع الفجر إلى وقت الضحى {وعشيا} هو من وقت زوال الشمس إلى أن تغرب

rows.speaker: أبو العالية
rows.claim: Abu al-Aliya interprets morning and evening as the dawn and afternoon prayers, or as praising God at both ends of the day.
rows.anchor: عن أبي العالية أن المراد بهما صلاة الفجر وصلاة العصر أو نزهوا ربكم طرفي النهار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bursevi prefers that Zakariyya ordered thanksgiving through glorification: the wondrous conception shows God can create a child despite the couple's age, and a saying recommends subhan Allah at wonders.
rows.anchor: هو الظاهر لأن معنى التسبيح في هذه الموضع تنزيه الله تعالى عن العجز عن خلق ولد

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: The inward reading sees honors in God calling him by name, naming John before birth, and giving him a unique name in form and meaning; John never desired or intended sin.
rows.anchor: منها : أنه تعالى ناداه باسمه زكريا وهذه كرامة منه. ومنها : أنه سماه يحيى ولم يجعل له

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: The reading says God inspires each person's name before creation, as Jesus announced a later messenger named Ahmad.
rows.anchor: إشارة إلى أنه تعالى يتولى تسمية كل إنسان قبل خلقه وما سمي أحد إلا بإلهام الله

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: The story contrasts the usual divine custom of creating something from something with God's power to create from nothing; both restoration of ordinary causes and creation without them were easy for God.
rows.anchor: أسباب حصول الولد منفية من الوالدين بالعقر والكبر وهي من السنة الإلهية فإن من السنة

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: The inward reading understands the spirit as created before the body by God's command, citing the statement that the spirit belongs to God's command.
rows.anchor: {قل الروح من أمر ربي} (الإسراء : 85) وهو أول مقدور تعلقت القدرة به

rows.speaker: المثنوي
rows.claim: The cited poem says creation can proceed without visible causes, like water emerging from nothing beyond the rule of water and air.
rows.anchor: وفي "المثنوي" :

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: يا يحيى is introduced as an ellipsis of God's speech: He granted John and said, O John.
rows.anchor: ووهبنا له يحيى وقلنا له يا يحيى

rows.speaker: الكاشفي
rows.claim: Kashifi says the sign lasted three days, then Zakariyya recovered; after gestation John was born and practiced ascetic worship while young, before revelation came to him.
rows.anchor: بعد از مضى مدت حمل متولد شد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Book is the Torah; taking it with strength means earnestness, resolve, and support through divine enabling.
rows.anchor: {خذ الكتاب} أي : التوراة {بقوة} بجد واستظهار بالتوفيق والتأييد

rows.speaker: الجلالين
rows.claim: Jalalayn glosses the command as God giving John the Torah and strengthening him to memorize and act on it.
rows.anchor: وقويتك على حفظها والعمل بما فيها

rows.speaker: المولى الجامي
rows.claim: Jami says an unseen divine power enabled Zakariyya and his wife to conceive despite ordinary causes; that power passed from them to John.
rows.anchor: لولا إمداد الحق زكريا وزوجته بقوة غيبية ربانية خارجة عن الأسباب المعتادة

rows.speaker: الأسئلة المقحمة
rows.claim: A theological question asks how this proves the Mu'tazilite position; the answer says 'his name is John' and then addressing him by that name shows name and named person are one.
rows.anchor: ثم نادى الشخص فقال : يا يحيى

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says الحكم means prophethood, granted when John was three or seven; another view takes it as wisdom, Torah comprehension, and religious understanding.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس : الحكم النبوة استنبأه الله تعالى وهو ابن ثلاث سنين أو سبع

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: When other children invited him to play, John replied that they were not created for play; Kashifi uses the episode to warn against wasting precious life in heedlessness.
rows.anchor: ما للعب خلقنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: حنانا is joined to الحكم, with its indefinite form magnifying it; the word moves from longing to compassion and mercy, either God's great mercy for John or mercy placed in his heart for others.
rows.anchor: {وحنانا من لدنا} عطف على الحكم وتنوينه للتفخيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zakat can mean purity from sin, charity God gave to his parents, or that God enabled John to give charity.
rows.anchor: طهارة من الذنوب

rows.speaker: الإمام
rows.claim: The Imam says compassion did not lead John to neglect an obligation; God joined kindness with freedom from failures in duty, as 24:2 warns against misplaced pity.
rows.anchor: لم تدعه شفقته إلى الإخلال بواجب لأن الرأفة ربما أورثت ترك الواجب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: John was obedient and avoided sins; he neither committed a sin nor even intended one.
rows.anchor: {وكان تقيا} مطيعا متجنبا عن المعاصي لم يعمل خطيئة ولم يهم بها قط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Being dutiful to his parents means being gentle and beneficent toward them.
rows.anchor: {وبرا بوالديه} عطف على تقيا أي : بارا بهما لطيفا بهما محسنا إليهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: John was neither arrogant nor disobedient to his parents, and was not rebellious against his Lord.
rows.anchor: {ولم يكن جبارا عصيا} متكبرا عاقا لهما أو عاصيا لربه

rows.speaker: بحر العلوم
rows.claim: Bahr al-Ulum defines جبار as arrogant, or as one who strikes or kills in anger without considering consequences, or as one too proud to humble himself before God's command.
rows.anchor: الجبار المتكبر وقيل هو الذي يضرب ويقتل على الغضب لا ينظر في العواقب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Peace means God's safety and protection for John in the most frightening passages; a nominal sentence expresses its enduring stability through them.
rows.anchor: سلامة من الله تعالى وأمان {عليه} على يحيى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At birth John is protected from Satan's sting, at death from death's terror and grave punishment, and at resurrection from the terror of Judgment and Hell.
rows.anchor: {يوم ولد} من رحم أمه من طعن الشيطان كما يطعن سائر بني آدم {ويوم يموت}

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: The inward reading makes birth emergence from nature, death annihilation of nature's demands in God, and resurrection subsistence after annihilation.
rows.anchor: إشارة إلى الولادة من أم الطبيعة والموت بالفناء عن مقتضيات الطبيعة في الله والبعث بالبقاء بعد الفناء

rows.speaker: ابن أبي عيينة
rows.claim: Ibn Abi Uyayna says birth, death, and resurrection are a person's loneliest moments: each brings him into an unfamiliar state, so John was singled out for peace in them.
rows.anchor: أوحش ما يكون الإنسان في هذه الأحوال يوم ولد فيخرج مما كان ويوم يموت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bursevi begins an inward allegory: Zakariyya is the human spirit, his wife the bodily frame, and John the heart receptive to divine effusion after the spirit doubts such a heart can arise from long bodily attachment.
rows.anchor: زكريا إشارة إلى الروح الإنساني وامرأته إلى الجثة الجسدانية التي هي زوج الروح ويحيى إلى القلب

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: In the inward reading, the spirit asks for a sign to learn how a barren bodily frame can carry the living heart; refusing to address or attend to three classes of created things draws the heart's divine light.
rows.anchor: لا تخاطب غير الله ولا تلتفت إلى ما سوى الله ثلاث ليال وبها يشير إلى مراتب ما سوى الله

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: The three classes are inanimate things, animals, and spiritual beings; the spirit leaves the sanctuary of its desire and tells its self-qualities, heart, and ego to face God through all times.
rows.anchor: وهي ثلاث : الجمادات ، والحيوانات ، والروحانيات

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: The living heart receives the book of divine effusion by God's power rather than weak human power and becomes knowing, wise, merciful, pure of attachment to other-than-God, and pious.
rows.anchor: يا يحيى خذ كتاب الفيض الإلهي بقوة ربانية لا بقوة إنسانية لأنه خلق الإنسان ضعيفا

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: The heart honors the spirit by illuminating it with divine effusion: the subtle spirit receives but cannot retain the flow, whereas the heart's clarity receives it and its density holds it.
rows.anchor: بل يعبر عنه الفيض ويقبله القلب ويمسكه لأن فيه صفاء وكثافة

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: This receptivity and retention is one secret of the trust humanity accepted while angels did not; the heart honors the body by using it according to Sharia commands and prohibitions, saving it from grave punishment and leading it to Paradise.
rows.anchor: وهذا أحد أسرار حمل الأمانة التي حملها الإنسان ولم تحملها الملائكة وأما بره بوالدة القالب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An unnamed saint recounts meeting a man in the wilderness of the Israelites, intuiting that he was al-Khidr, and beginning to question him; the account breaks off here.
rows.anchor: كنت في تيه بني إسرائيل فإذا رجل يماشيني فتعجبت منه وألهمت أنه الخضر
